# Logos

The primary single-line `Enterprise Solutions | MAP` lockup, in the only two colourways that exist: Navy for
light grounds, White for Navy grounds and the cover badge. The "WPP" letters are built from halftone dots;
"Enterprise Solutions" is solid.

**Ink:** `WPP_ES_MAP_logo_NAVY.svg` is filled `#000050` (`wpp-navy`); the White variant is `#FFFFFF`. The fill
is set on each shape, never in a `<style>` block: an upload strips `<style>`, which is what turned the first
uploads of these files black. So they keep their colour as images, here and in a deck.

## Rules

- **Navy or White only.** No other colourway exists, and no recolouring.
- **Safe space: the width of the second "P" of WPP**, on all sides.
- Never stretch, rotate, outline or place on a busy ground.
- Double-stacked and triple-stacked variants exist in the wider brand system but do not ship here — a deck
  needs only the primary lockup. Print, CMYK and Pantone variants do not ship either.
- Sub-brand and partner logos are created centrally. Partner co-branding runs partner logo · navy dot
  separator · WPP ES logo, at equal visual weight.

## In a deck

The logo appears small and bottom-right: either as the Bold 16px text footer line, or on a cover inside the
solid Navy badge flush to the bottom-right corner. In Claude Design Slides, copy the file into the deck and
place it as an `<img>`. The HTML generator inlines the SVG as an `<svg>` element instead: a self-contained
deck never references a logo by path.

> **Proprietary.** WPP trademark. Use is governed by the brand guideline; not for redistribution.

# Icons

32 brand icons, each built from dots on a rounded-square grid: the glyph outline drawn as a string of solid
circles of varying diameter, with a loose scatter of tiny satellite dots around it.

**Ink:** every file is normalized to `currentColor` so it recolours in CSS. That means these tiles render in
the browser's default ink rather than `wpp-navy` — in use the icon host sets the colour: 44px `wpp-navy` by
default, `.icon--lg` at 64px, `.icon--orange` for the one sanctioned orange moment, auto-flipping to
`wpp-cream` on navy slides and panels.

## Three weight families

**line** (monoline, 96px) — `brain` · `chart-decline` · `checklist` · `flow` · `mind` · `network` · `reach` ·
`segments` · `strength`

**solid** (96px) — `audience` · `clipboard` · `cycle` · `energy` · `globe` · `globe-grid` · `globe-hands` ·
`growth` · `idea` · `loop` · `puzzle` · `report` · `rocket` · `team` · `thought` · `workflow`

**bold** (rounded, 24px) — `face-sad` · `gift` · `hands-care` · `heart-mail` · `trophy`

**accents** — `spark` · `spark-bold`

## Where the filename misleads

| File | What it actually is |
|---|---|
| `brain` | Gears inside a head |
| `chart-decline` | Bars with a **downward** arrow — cost and risk reduction only, never growth |
| `mind` | The **AI icon** — a circuit head |
| `network` | Three linked user nodes, the same drawing as `segments` |
| `reach` | A person inside radar arcs — audience and reach |
| `segments` | Three linked user nodes — segmentation |
| `globe-hands` | An Americas globe. There are no hands. |
| `globe-grid` | A thinner near-duplicate of `globe` |
| `hands-care` | Hands holding a gem — value, premium |
| `loop` | Nodes cycling — test and learn |
| `strength` | A weightlifter. Capability slides only, and only if the tone can take it. |
| `workflow` | The same glyph as `flow`, in the solid style |

Four pairs of files are one drawing each: `audience` and `team` (a group under a speech panel), `clipboard`
and `report` (a clipboard with a pencil), `network` and `segments`, `cycle` and `loop` (nodes cycling). Either
name renders the same glyph.

## The pairing rule is hard

**One weight family per icon row, per slide.** A monoline icon beside a solid one reads as two different icon
sets — the most visible amateur tell in the system. Deck-wide default is **solid**; use **line** only when
every icon on the slide is line, **bold** only in hosts of 44px or more. Where both styles of a glyph exist,
the family decides for you.

`spark` and `spark-bold` are accents, not bullets: maximum two per deck, in statement-adjacent air only.

## Known gaps

These have no suite icon and degrade to the dot bullet by design — they do not exist in the brand source:
calendar/timeline, money/ROI, shield/security, target/goal, search, gear alone, lone user, warning,
integration/API, database, commerce/cart.

**Never substitute a generic icon library.** The dot bullet is always safe.

# Illustrations

Thirteen dot-halftone motifs: eleven WPP Open and MAP motifs plus two conversions on the canonical square
grid. One colour per illustration, flat ground, anchored to an edge or corner and cropped, leaving clear space
for type.

**Ink:** Navy motifs are `wpp-navy`; `_Orange` files are the sanctioned orange colourways, in Orange 700
(`MAP_Mountain-01_Orange.png` and `MAP_Peaks-01_Orange.png` measure a slightly warmer `#EE8031`). Never recolour
a navy PNG by hand — use the shipped orange file.

## The Rocks and Ribbon trap

The nine 1920px-class and conversion files have **fully transparent grounds**, so the Cream field shows
through. The four 964 × 540 EMF-sourced files — Rocks and Ribbon, both colourways — **do not**: they carry a
baked opaque cream field around the ink. On Navy, on a tinted panel or over a photo they print their own
background as pale wedges.

Navy ink disappearing on Navy is the failure everyone expects. This is the one that gets shipped, because the
slide looks populated. Keep them on Cream, as accents no taller than 640px — never full-bleed, never covers.
The verifier warns when a 964px asset lands in a host of 1100px or more.

Rocks and Ribbon go with the comparison layout (ComparisonV1), in the colourway of the deck's motif family. As
that layout's centrepiece they do not count against the one-motif-family rule.

## The canonical settings

Min dot 2.0px · max dot 8.0px · square grid · spacing 10.0px · contrast 1.00 · jitter 0.00 · size variation
0.00. Pipeline: source image → dot generator → subject-only dots, background cleaned → recolour. The legacy
WPP Open motifs use a hexagonal pattern; both are sanctioned, and new conversions use the square grid.

Place motifs **behind** text, and never let body copy sit over the dense part of a halftone.

> **Proprietary.** WPP Open and MAP artwork. Not for redistribution.

# Photography

Thirteen photographs, **already navy-duotone**, mined from the MAP brand deck. Ten are cut-outs with
transparent grounds; three are full-bleed. They exist so no photo slot ever has to render as a grey box — a
brief-supplied photo still wins when there is one.

**Ink:** these are pre-duotoned. Never wrap one in `.duo` again.

| File | Subject | Metaphor | Form |
|---|---|---|---|
| `photo-lighthouse.png` | Lighthouse on a rocky islet | guidance, direction | cut-out 1150px |
| `photo-handoff.webp` | Hands passing a relay baton | handoff, partnership | cut-out 1200px |
| `photo-confetti.png` | Falling confetti | celebration, launch | cut-out 1100px |
| `photo-chess.png` | Row of chess pieces | strategy, precision | cut-out 1200px |
| `photo-globe.png` | Stippled engraving globe | global, markets | cut-out 820px |
| `photo-pencils.png` | Hand fanning pencils | creativity, options | cut-out 1050px |
| `photo-dancers.png` | Dancers' feet mid-step | momentum, craft | cut-out 1050px |
| `photo-gears.png` | Interlocking halftone gears | integration, systems | cut-out 900px |
| `photo-fibers.png` | Fibre-optic wisps and nodes | connectivity, data flow | cut-out 1150px |
| `photo-team.webp` | Six people arm-in-arm, from behind | teamwork, alignment | cut-out 1000px |
| `photo-diver.jpg` | Diver under a sunlit surface | exploration, depth | full-bleed 1600px |
| `photo-fjord.jpg` | Misty fjord, mirror water | clarity, journey | full-bleed 1600px |
| `photo-ridge.jpg` | Layered mountain ridge | ascent, long view | full-bleed 1600px |

## Rules

- Cut-outs sit on Cream or White like halftone motifs; full-bleeds fill a panel or bleed host.
- **Respect the native widths.** The verifier warns on upscales.
- **One photo moment per six slides**, unless the deck direction is high-impact. It counts as a dark moment.
- Text never sits on a duotone — it owns the other half of the composition.
- Pick by metaphor, not by how the picture looks.

## Licence — action required

> The repository's `NOTICE.md` records that these 13 files **were carried over without a recorded source or
> licence**. Before any of them appears in a client-facing or externally published deck, confirm the licence
> for that specific image and record it.
>
> Internal decks may use them under the same assumption they were used before. This is a documentation gap,
> not a known infringement — but it is unresolved, and it travels with this system.

# Textures

Two full-bleed 1920 × 1080 dot-field textures, quantized to the brand ramp.

| File | Feel |
|---|---|
| `contours-cream.png` | Cream topographic contour lines in slate-navy dots — a tactile paper layer for the editorial-quiet direction; it rhymes with the "map" in MAP. |
| `orbs-cream.png` | Soft navy halftone orbs on cream — quiet depth behind a statement moment. |

## Rules

They are **backdrops, not ink**. Place one under a whole slide at the bottom of the stack.

- **One texture moment per deck, maximum.**
- Never behind dense body copy.
- Never as a panel fill or a decorative patch — they are full-bleed grounds or nothing.

# Exemplars

Four reference renders, one per deck **direction** — the registered choice that sets a deck's divider
colourway, motion level and overall temperature.

| File | Direction | Character |
|---|---|---|
| `editorial-quiet.png` | editorial-quiet | The calm default: orange colourway, subtle motion, lots of air |
| `data-forward.png` | data-forward | Numbers carry the argument: orange colourway, subtle motion |
| `statement-led.png` | statement-led | Big type carries it: navy-dots colourway, full motion |
| `high-impact.png` | high-impact | Navy-full colourway, full motion, poster moments allowed |

These are **not templates.** They are the target a finished deck is judged against — the reason the direction
is a registered choice rather than a per-slide decision. Pick the direction first; it then decides the
divider colourway, the motion level and how often a dark moment or a photo is allowed.
